result.summary: The image depicts a wide urban street with sidewalks on both sides and a marked crosswalk. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the wide crossing distance and faded pavement markings increase exposure to vehicular traffic.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The transverse lines of the crosswalk are significantly worn, reducing visibility to approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Pavement Degradation
hazards.description: Visible patching and cracking in the roadway surface near the crossing area.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground in the middle of the lane

hazards.name: Wide Unprotected Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes without a refuge island, increasing exposure time.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Replace faded transverse markings with continental or ladder-style high-visibility markings.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the crossing to reduce the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a high-visibility continental crosswalk and curb ramps with tactile paving at a signalized intersection. However, the three-lane one-way roadway increases pedestrian exposure and potential vehicle speeds, while the lack of a median or curb extensions leaves pedestrians unprotected during the crossing. Street trees and clear sidewalks enhance the walking environment, but additional traffic calming measures are absent.

hazards.name: Multi-lane one-way roadway
hazards.description: Three lanes of one-way traffic can encourage higher vehicle speeds and increase the risk of multi-threat crashes where one car stops but another does not.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian refuge
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the entire width of the three-lane street in one stage without a protected waiting area.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection corners to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian refuge island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross the roadway in stages.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light, reducing conflicts with turning traffic.

result.summary: The intersection features a patterned crosswalk and curb ramps with tactile warning strips, indicating a baseline level of pedestrian accommodation. However, visibility is compromised by parked vehicles near the crossing, and there are no visible pedestrian-specific signals or physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the left side of the street are located very close to the crosswalk, which can hide pedestrians from oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street, immediately before the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Removing parking spaces near the intersection to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extending the sidewalk into the parking lane to reduce crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized urban intersection with high-visibility crosswalk markings and basic pedestrian infrastructure. While sidewalks and signals are present, the wide roadway and lack of physical refuge islands or curb extensions increase pedestrian exposure to traffic.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide multi-lane roadway increases the time pedestrians are exposed to vehicle traffic without a refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Wide Turning Radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry appears to allow vehicles to make right turns at higher speeds.
